1: The officials credit the cameras alone, even though road repairs and new crossings happened at the same time. It assumes only one factor caused the drop — B.
2: The developers 'claim that their product significantly improves users' overall well-being' — C. The survey results support it; D is a counterpoint.
3: Rates: 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6 of the job per hour, so 6 hours.
4: More homework will raise scores only if students can actually do it at home — A.
5: Most people prefer online shopping and big retailers are closing stores and investing online. So online shopping is popular and changing business strategy — C.
6: Critics say the drop may be temporary or seasonal. B answers them: landfill waste has kept falling for several years.
7: Structure: X requires Y; Y won't happen; so X won't happen. D matches: a happy marriage requires talking more; they can't; so it won't be happy.
8: 80 × 60 = 4800 m²; a diagonal splits it into two equal triangles of 2400 m².
9: Only already-satisfied customers were asked, so the sample is biased — A.
10: A day off will raise turnout only if work is what stops people voting — A.

14: Tested only on under-40s, so the results may not apply to older users — the very people anti-ageing cream targets (B).

19: John's prizes: crossword £30–45, logic puzzle £10–15, mental arithmetic £30–35. Largest gap: £45 − £10 = £35.
20: The cut only removes a small corner, so looking straight at any face you still see a full square outline. B shows a square with a corner missing, which can't happen. D (a square with a line across a corner) is the view of a face next to the cut.
21: Greener areas had cooler air, cleaner air and less stress, so green spaces improve urban living conditions — C. The others go beyond the passage.

23: Email-free hours help only if people work better when they can concentrate without interruptions — C.
24: The report says breakfast prevents weight gain. A gives another explanation: some breakfast-eaters also followed diet and exercise plans.
25: Officials credit the bikes, but public transport ridership rose a lot at the same time — another reason car use fell (A).

28: The graph is flat (fixed salary) up to a point, then rises steadily: a fixed amount plus a percentage of sales above a target — D.
